labels.label: def:yamabe

hypotheses.note: measured model with n = 0 boundary components (DEC-186); N ≥ 3 where used
through the conformal law eq:conformal-energy (confEnergy), as Yamabe.Kobayashi; closed_confEnergy shows it is the printed right side l.177–179 when n = 0
over a supplied family rep : Cls → CurvedMetric X N, packaged as a ClosedConformal (kb/0083: the sup over all CurvedMetrics is unbounded, Real.sSup junk 0)

findings: eq:yamabe-energy's second equality EH = ⟨R_g⟩ Vol^{2/N} (l.163) holds for every volume, both sides 0 when Vol = 0 (closedEH_eq_avg); nothing wrong in the paper.
questions: σ(Σ) (l.170): 'all conformal classes of Riemannian metrics' has no counterpart in the model. Reading taken: σ over a supplied family of class representatives (yamabeClasses); Y_le_sigma needs the family bounded above (Aubin's bound, thm:yamabe (a), not formalized).

labels.label: prop:csc-yamabe

hypotheses.note: ∀ x, R x = c in (b) and the assembly; weakened to vol-a.e. in csc_yamabe_a

hypotheses.paper: Σ nonempty (implicit: a manifold of dimension N)
hypotheses.note: vol_g ≠ 0 (μ ≠ 0 on a manifold) in (b); without it Y = sInf ∅ = 0
SobolevIneq on a bare model; discharged sorry-free on a model reading a compact manifold (Mfd.Reads.csc_yamabe_b, prop_csc_yamabe via Mfd.Reads.sobolevIneq)

hypotheses.paper: uniqueness up to homotheties (LeeParker1987, Schoen1989, maximum principle)
hypotheses.note: named Prop CSCUnique (constant scalar curvature metric read as a positive weak solution of the Yamabe equation, YamabeEq; homothety as u constant), a hypothesis hU, never an axiom

no counterpart in the model; 'the inequality may be strict' is witnessed on the connected closed two-point model with R ≡ 100 (toyClosed_csc_not_yamabe: Y ≤ 114 < 120 ≤ EH), a model fact, not Schoen's example

findings: prop:csc-yamabe (a), l.195, uniqueness: as printed it does not hold when R_g ≡ 0 and Σ is disconnected. 'Closed' at l.161 is 'compact, without boundary', with no connectedness. Example: flat T³ ⊔ T³ with u = 1 on one torus and u = 2 on the other. The metric u^4 g is flat, so it has constant scalar curvature, lies in [g], and is not homothetic to g (argued on manifolds). In Lean: toyClosedCut_not_cscUnique, the closed two-point model with d = 0 and R ≡ 0, u = (2,1), c' = 0. On the connected closed two-point model it holds (toyClosed_cscUnique). For R_g ≡ c < 0 disconnectedness does no harm. Suggested fix: add 'connected' to the hypotheses of prop:csc-yamabe or to the convention at l.161. The first assertions of (a) and (b) need no connectedness.
questions: Is Σ assumed connected throughout § 2 (l.161)? Reading taken: no, as printed. The uniqueness is carried as stated by the paper, and its failure in the disconnected case is recorded as a finding.

The uniqueness in (a): reading of 'constant scalar curvature metric in [g]' on the model as a positive weak solution of -a_N Δu + R_g u = c' u^{p*-1} against every v ∈ D, with ⟨∇u,∇v⟩ by polarisation of the Dirichlet energy (the model cannot compute the curvature of u^{4/(N-2)} g, kb/0018).

kb_proposals: A closed leaf is a MeasuredModel with n = 0. closed_minimal (fun j => j.elim0) supplies MinimalBoundary, so every lem:kobayashi result applies verbatim, and Mfd.Reads with σ : Fin 0 → Measure discharges the Sobolev inequality (YamabeScaffold.ClosedLeaves).

The cut closed two-point model (toyClosed with d := 0) tests whether a statement needs Σ connected. With R ≡ 0 every positive u solves the weak Yamabe equation with c' = 0, so the uniqueness of prop:csc-yamabe (a) fails there (toyClosedCut_not_cscUnique).
notes: No strict file edited. The module imports only strict modules (Yamabe.External, Yamabe.ManifoldTheorems, Yamabe.Negative), so it can graduate as a file move. Both rows stay partial and unmarked. def:yamabe is partial because of the σ reading and the conformal-law reading of Y. prop:csc-yamabe is partial because the uniqueness is a carried cited input and Schoen's examples are not formalized. The first assertions of (a) and (b) are proved, sorry-free, on a model reading a compact manifold. Downstream T-yamabe-gap-corollaries can use Y_le_sigma ('Y ≤ σ by definition') and csc_yamabe_a. The axioms of the 12 principal declarations were checked through a /tmp copy: standard only.
